headline: 12 people jailed as attack on Radda Health Centre sparks outrage
summary: A court has sent two more suspects to jail, bringing the total to 12, following a violent raid on a mother and child health center in Mirpur.
details: A Dhaka court has sent two more suspects, Minu (35) and Milon (45), to jail in connection with the attack on the Radda MCH-FP center in Mirpur's Shah Ali area.
The incident occurred around midnight on a Thursday, when a group of attackers armed with hammers, sticks, and local weapons stormed the facility.
Two security guards were beaten and detained by the attackers, who then used an excavator to demolish parts of the semi-permanent structure.
The raid resulted in approximately 49 lakh BDT in damages to the facility's registration, laboratory, ultrasound, and vaccination centers.
Valuable medical equipment, including two ultrasound machines, a generator, computers, printers, and refrigerators, were looted from the center.
Jamaat-e-Islami has announced a donation of 50 lakh BDT to help restore and resume the operations of the Radda Health Centre.
Interim government advisor Asif Mahmud has stated that this attack was not an isolated incident, but part of a wider pattern of illegal occupations across the country.
Executive Director Dr. Nasrin Akhtar filed the case following the devastation of the essential maternal and child healthcare facility.
caption:
An excavator was used to demolish a mother and child health center in Mirpur. 12 suspects are now behind bars.

A Dhaka court has sent two more suspects, Minu (35) and Milon (45), to jail in connection with the attack on the Radda MCH-FP center in Mirpur's Shah Ali area.

The incident occurred around midnight on a Thursday, when a group of attackers armed with hammers, sticks, and local weapons stormed the facility.

Two security guards were beaten and detained by the attackers, who then used an excavator to demolish parts of the semi-permanent structure.

The raid resulted in approximately 49 lakh BDT in damages to the facility's registration, laboratory, ultrasound, and vaccination centers.

Valuable medical equipment, including two ultrasound machines, a generator, computers, printers, and refrigerators, were looted from the center.

Jamaat-e-Islami has announced a donation of 50 lakh BDT to help restore and resume the operations of the Radda Health Centre.

Interim government advisor Asif Mahmud has stated that this attack was not an isolated incident, but part of a wider pattern of illegal occupations across the country.

Executive Director Dr. Nasrin Akhtar filed the case following the devastation of the essential maternal and child healthcare facility.

headline: Jamaat MP's son-in-law arrested over attack on Salman Muqtadir's studio
summary: Mizanur Rahman was picked up by DB police from his Dhaka home in connection with the vandalism of a building housing the content creator's studio.
details: Mizanur Rahman, 59, the son-in-law of Jamaat-e-Islami lawmaker Md Abdul Gafur, was arrested by the DB Gulshan Division on Monday.
A team of police picked him up from his residence in Dhaka's Paschim Matikata around 5:00 PM.
The arrest is linked to a case filed over an attack on New Gini Properties in the ECB Chattar area of Dhaka.
According to police, the building was targeted and the studio of content creator Salman Muqtadir, who rented a floor there, was vandalised during the attack.
Mizanur Rahman is listed as accused number 9 in the case filed with the Cantonment Police Station on September 27.
caption:
A Jamaat MP's son-in-law has been arrested for his alleged involvement in an attack on Salman Muqtadir's studio.

Mizanur Rahman, 59, the son-in-law of Jamaat-e-Islami lawmaker Md Abdul Gafur, was arrested by the DB Gulshan Division on Monday.

A team of police picked him up from his residence in Dhaka's Paschim Matikata around 5:00 PM.

The arrest is linked to a case filed over an attack on New Gini Properties in the ECB Chattar area of Dhaka.

According to police, the building was targeted and the studio of content creator Salman Muqtadir, who rented a floor there, was vandalised during the attack.

Mizanur Rahman is listed as accused number 9 in the case filed with the Cantonment Police Station on September 27.
